findings.title: Local cache is set before the DB write, so a device rejected by the limit is let in on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` (line 87) before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 93). When the limit is reached, the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and `Authenticate` rejects that request. The key is already cached, though (TTL 29 min, impl.go:42). The device's next request hits the cache at line 83 and `TagDevice` returns nil. `Anonymous.Authenticate` (client.go:44-52) then returns an anonymous identity. A rejected device is therefore blocked once and admitted on retry for the next 29 minutes on that instance, so the limit is not enforced. Set the cache key only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or delete it when the call returns an error.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so the limit can be exceeded under concurrency
findings.body: `CountDevices` (line 110) and the upsert (lines 120-153) run in separate sessions with no lock. Concurrent first requests from several new devices, or from several Grafana instances sharing the DB, can all see `count < limit` and all insert. The limit is soft. If that is acceptable, say so in the config docs. Otherwise do the check inside the insert, for example `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit`. This also adds a COUNT query for every uncached device when the limit is set.

findings.title: Tagging is now synchronous on the request path
findings.body: The goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and recover is gone. Every uncached anonymous request now waits on the DB (a COUNT plus an upsert when the limit is set) using the request context. A client that cancels the request also cancels the write. Synchronous tagging is needed so the limit error can reject the request. Even so, with no limit configured (`deviceLimit == 0`) this still adds DB latency to the auth path for no benefit. Consider keeping the async path when the limit is disabled.

findings.title: Limit test misses the key behaviours
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only checks that a second new device is rejected. It does not check that an already-registered device can still update when the limit is reached, which is the stated purpose of `updateDevice`. It does not check a device whose `updated_at` is outside the 30-day window. There is no test in `anonimpl` that `Anonymous.Authenticate` returns an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and still succeeds on other tag errors. There is no test for the cache path described in the other finding.

findings.title: Dead wire provider and duplicated expiration constants
findings.body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes an `int64`, and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` builds the store itself. `pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and the `AnonStore` binding. Nothing consumes them any more, and the provider needs an `int64` that wire cannot supply, so any new consumer of the binding would fail wire generation. Remove them. The 30-day expiration is now defined three times: `anonstore/database.go:16`, `api/api.go:18` and `impl.go:25` (`thirtyDays`). Export one constant and reuse it.

findings.title: New `device_limit` setting is undocumented
findings.body: `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` is read here, but `conf/defaults.ini` and `conf/sample.ini` (which list `hide_version` next to it) and the docs do not mention it. Add the setting to both ini files and to the anonymous auth docs, and note that 0 means unlimited.

findings.title: Frontend default does not match what the backend sends
findings.body: The backend DTO sends `anonymousDeviceLimit` as a plain `int64` (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195), so it is always a number, with 0 meaning no limit. The frontend types it as `number | undefined` and defaults it to `undefined`. In the class, `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` is inferred as type `undefined` and not `number | undefined`. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`, or use `number` with default 0.

contracts.action: Anonymous Authenticate now tags the device synchronously and rejects the request when the device limit is reached
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous path: fire-and-forget goroutine with a 2-minute timeout that only logged errors. Authn service joins client errors and returns them (pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/service.go:197-222). The context handler stores them in LookupTokenErr (pkg/services/contexthandler/contexthandler.go:116-124).
contracts.before_after: Before: tag errors never affected auth. After: ErrDeviceLimitReached makes Authenticate return nil, err, so the request is not anonymous. Other tag errors are still only logged. The first rejected request is blocked, but TagDevice's local cache entry is already set (impl.go:87), so later requests from the same device pass.
contracts.visible_effect: The new device gets an auth failure on its first request only. Within 29 minutes the same device is let in on that instance.
contracts.failure_mode: The DB error on COUNT or UPDATE is returned from TagDevice. A non-limit error is logged and the user proceeds. A limit error is rejected once and then bypassed through the cache.

summary: The device limit can be bypassed. `tagDeviceUI` caches the device key before the DB write (impl.go:87), so a device rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is let in on its next request for 29 minutes. Smaller points: the count-then-insert is not atomic, tagging is now synchronous even when no limit is set, and the limit tests miss key behaviours. The new `device_limit` setting is undocumented in `conf/defaults.ini` and `conf/sample.ini`. The `wire.go` provider for the store is now dead, and the 30-day constant is duplicated three times. I only read the code; nothing was built or run.
